rules.principle: Encode quantitative (ratio/interval) data with position or size only, since these are Bertin's sole quantitative visual variables.
rules.applies_when: A data field typed as quantitative (continuous or ratio-scale numeric) is mapped to a visual channel in the design plan.

check.detail: For every plan encoding where field.type == 'quantitative', assert channel in {'x','y','position','size','length','area','radius'}. Flag if the quantitative field is carried by hue, shape, texture, orientation, or value alone.

rules.fix: Reassign the quantitative field to a positional channel (x/y) or size; demote the current channel to a secondary or categorical role.

rules.principle: Encode nominal (categorical, unordered) data with color hue or orientation, which are selective and associative, or with shape, which is associative; all three carry categories, but prefer hue or orientation when the reader must isolate a category at a glance, since shape alone is not selective.
rules.applies_when: A data field typed as nominal/categorical with no inherent order is mapped to a visual channel.

check.detail: For every plan encoding where field.type == 'nominal', assert channel in {'hue','color','shape','symbol','orientation'} or a discrete positional facet. Flag nominal fields mapped to size, value/lightness, or a continuous sequential scale.

rules.fix: Map the nominal field to hue or shape; if too many categories, group them or switch to small multiples.

rules.principle: Reserve color hue for nominal categories only; never use hue to encode an ordered or quantitative field, because hue is not perceptually ordered.
rules.applies_when: A field mapped to the hue/color channel is typed as ordinal or quantitative, or the color scale is a rainbow/multi-hue gradient standing in for magnitude.

check.detail: In the plan, if channel == 'hue'/'color', assert the bound field.type == 'nominal'. Additionally scan the SVG/scale definition: flag a color scale that interpolates across multiple distinct hues (e.g. rainbow) while bound to a numeric domain.

rules.fix: Replace the multi-hue gradient with a single-hue sequential value (lightness) scale for quantitative data, or a two-hue diverging value scale for signed data; keep hue only for the categorical dimension.

rules.principle: Encode ordinal or quantitative magnitude carried by color with value (lightness), not hue, since value is Bertin's ordered retinal variable.
rules.applies_when: The design intends to convey rank or magnitude through a color channel (choropleth, heatmap, shaded encoding).

check.detail: For any encoding where field.type in {'ordinal','quantitative'} and the channel is color-based, assert the scale varies primarily in lightness/value (single-hue sequential or two-hue diverging) rather than hue. Inspect scale type == 'sequential' or 'diverging'.

rules.fix: Switch the color scale to a sequential (one hue, dark-to-light) or diverging (two hues, dark-light-dark) value ramp such as a ColorBrewer sequential/diverging palette.

rules.principle: Match every encoding's visual-variable organization level to the data type: nominal needs a selective variable, ordinal needs an ordered variable, quantitative needs a quantitative variable.
rules.applies_when: Any field-to-channel mapping exists in the design plan.

check.detail: Build a lookup: quantitative variables={position,size}; ordered variables={position,size,value,grain/texture}; selective variables={all except shape}. For each encoding assert the channel's max organization level >= the field's required level (quantitative>ordered>selective/nominal).

rules.fix: Promote the field to a channel whose organization level meets or exceeds the data type's requirement (e.g. move an ordinal field off hue onto value or position).

rules.principle: Do not use shape to distinguish categories that must be scanned as a group, because shape is the one visual variable Bertin classified as non-selective.
rules.applies_when: A nominal field is encoded by marker shape/symbol and the task requires isolating or counting all members of one category at a glance.

check.detail: On the rendered SVG, verify that a single shape-coded category can be visually grouped without serial search; if the reader must inspect markers one by one to find a category, the shape encoding fails selectivity.

rules.fix: Re-encode the grouping category with hue (selective) and keep shape only as a redundant or secondary cue.

rules.principle: Keep the number of distinguishable hue categories within perceptual limits (roughly 7, hard cap ~12); beyond that, hue stops being selective.
rules.applies_when: A nominal field with many distinct values is mapped to color hue.

check.detail: Count distinct categories bound to the hue channel; flag when count > 7 (warn) and count > 12 (fail).

rules.fix: Aggregate minor categories into an 'other' bin, use small multiples/faceting, or add position/label redundancy so categories no longer rely on hue alone.

rules.principle: Encode a single data attribute per visual variable per mark, unless redundant encoding is deliberate; Bertin treats each retinal variable as one independent dimension.
rules.applies_when: The design plan binds two or more distinct, unrelated data fields to the same visual variable on the same mark.

check.detail: Group plan encodings by channel; flag any channel bound to more than one distinct field unless the encoding is explicitly marked redundant (same field, two channels is allowed and encouraged).

rules.fix: Assign each extra attribute to a separate free visual variable, or drop the overloaded dimension; convert to small multiples if variables are exhausted.

rules.principle: Order the visual sequence of an ordinal encoding to match the data order, since an ordered visual variable must present a clear linear progression.
rules.applies_when: An ordinal field is encoded by value/lightness, size, or a discrete categorical color/position scale.

check.detail: For ordinal encodings, assert the scale's output range is monotonic in the ordered variable (lightness increases/decreases monotonically, sizes increase with rank, category order in the domain matches the data's defined order).

rules.fix: Sort the scale domain to the field's natural order and use a monotonic value/size ramp so the visual progression tracks the data order.

rules.principle: Prefer position over all other variables when accuracy of quantitative comparison matters, as position is the most precise of Bertin's quantitative variables.
rules.applies_when: The primary analytical task is comparing quantitative values across marks (e.g. ranking, precise magnitude reading).

check.detail: Confirm the most important quantitative field is carried on a positional axis (x or y) rather than on size, area, or color; requires reading the design plan's stated task/intent against its primary encoding.

rules.fix: Restructure so the key quantitative comparison rides on a common-scale positional axis (e.g. convert a size-encoded bubble comparison to a bar or dot plot).

rules.principle: Avoid encoding quantitative data with area or 2D size scaled linearly by value, because area is a weaker quantitative channel that distorts perceived magnitude.
rules.applies_when: A quantitative field is mapped to a 2D mark's area, radius, or bubble size.

check.detail: If a quantitative field maps to a circle/area mark, assert the scale is area-proportional (radius = k * sqrt(value)), not radius-linear; flag radius-linear scaling and flag when position could have been used instead.

rules.fix: Use an area-proportional (sqrt) scale for size, or move the quantitative field to a positional/length channel where perception is more accurate.

rules.principle: Use texture/grain only for nominal or coarse ordinal distinctions and never as the sole carrier of precise quantitative values.
rules.applies_when: A field is encoded by texture, pattern, or grain (e.g. hatching density) in the design plan.

check.detail: If channel == 'texture'/'grain'/'pattern', assert field.type in {'nominal','ordinal'} and not 'quantitative'; flag any quantitative field relying solely on texture.

rules.fix: Reserve texture for categories or coarse ranks; move quantitative magnitude to position, size, or value.

rules.principle: Add redundant encoding (e.g. hue plus shape, or value plus position) for critical distinctions to survive grayscale printing and color-vision deficiency.
rules.applies_when: A category or ordinal distinction critical to the figure's message is carried by a single retinal variable, especially hue.

check.detail: Render the SVG in grayscale and, separately, under a deuteranopia simulation; verify the critical distinction remains legible. If categories collapse, the single-variable encoding is insufficient.

rules.fix: Add a second, orthogonal visual variable (shape, position, direct label, or value) as redundant reinforcement of the hue encoding.

rules.principle: Do not use hue or orientation differences to imply that unrelated categories have more or less importance, since these associative variables should keep all marks equally visible.
rules.applies_when: A nominal encoding uses hue or orientation and one category is rendered with markedly higher salience (saturation, size) without an intended emphasis reason.

check.detail: On the rendered figure, check that categories encoded by an associative variable read at comparable salience; flag when one nominal category unintentionally dominates because its color is far more saturated or its marks larger.

rules.fix: Equalize saturation/size across the associative categories, or if emphasis is intended, make it deliberate and add an annotation explaining the highlighted category.
